report:
**Conclusion:** High-quality medical evidence indicates that saw palmetto (*Serenoa repens*) preparations do **not** improve urinary symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) significantly more than placebo in the longer term.

### The Evidence

Although early observational and smaller studies suggested modest benefits, large-scale, well-controlled trials demonstrate no clinical efficacy over placebo:

* **Rigorous Long-Term Trials:** A landmark double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated saw palmetto over 1 year and found no significant differences between saw palmetto and placebo in lower urinary tract symptom scores, urinary flow rate, or prostate size (https://www.vumc.org/poison-control/toxicology-question-week/june-2-2021-does-saw-palmetto-improve-symptoms-benign-prostatic).
* **Escalating Dose Studies (CAMUS Trial):** A multi-center trial published in *JAMA* tested saw palmetto at up to three times the standard dose (up to 960 mg daily over 72 weeks). Even at higher doses, saw palmetto failed to outperform placebo in reducing urinary symptoms (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/1104439).
* **Systematic Reviews:** A Cochrane Systematic Review evaluated randomized clinical trials and concluded that saw palmetto monotherapy does not provide superior symptom reduction or urinary flow improvement compared with placebo (https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD001423_serenoa-repens-benign-prostatic-hyperplasia).
* **Health Authority Consensus:** The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) reports that high-quality evidence consistently shows saw palmetto is no more effective than a placebo for treating BPH symptoms (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/providers/digest/spotlight-on-saw-palmetto-science).
